extracted.intended_audience: researchers, funding-agency staff, and policymakers interested in grant peer review, rubric design, and bias in evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and designing external peer review criteria and rubrics for grant applications, and detecting/adjusting for demographic and linguistic biases in reviewer assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consistently invoke methodological rigor as a central evaluative dimension in external peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess study design, statistical methods, reproducibility, and appropriateness of methods for stated aims. Provide concrete methodological criticisms rather than vague statements. Note: emphasis on methodological rigor can interact with career stage and resources available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality or novelty of the proposed research is used as a key criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the proposal advances beyond the current state of the field and offers new concepts or approaches. Compare claimed novelty to discipline-specific norms to avoid penalizing incremental but important work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record / qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record and applicant qualifications (past publications, grants, achievements) are repeatedly used to judge proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh prior productivity, relevant expertise, and past successes. Be aware this criterion tends to favor senior applicants; consider balancing with measures that account for early-career potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility of the proposed work (likelihood of successful completion) is a common review criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity of methods, timeline, budget realism, and preliminary data when relevant. Explicitly consider how emphasis on preliminary data may disadvantage early-career applicants and whether alternative evidence of feasibility is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance to the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance or importance of the research question and potential impact is used to judge merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential scientific, societal or disciplinary impact. Provide specific reasons why the work matters rather than generic statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: International competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the project is internationally competitive is invoked by reviewers as an evaluative standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the proposal positions the researcher and institution to compete internationally, considering novelty, methods, and team. Avoid conflating country/institution reputation with intrinsic project quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and team adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of resources and the research team (skills, composition) is used to assess likelihood of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether requested resources, infrastructure, and team expertise match project needs. Distinguish between legitimate resource concerns and biases about institutional prestige or team composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final score (numerical evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The numeric final score assigned by the reviewer to the application is a primary quantitative outcome metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistently defined scales and scoring rubrics; track score distributions across applicant groups to detect systematic differences. Interpret small effect sizes in large samples carefully (statistical significance vs practical magnitude).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to fund (binary/categorical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an explicit recommendation to fund or not as a key decision input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture categorical recommendations in addition to scores; analyze how recommendations align with scores and whether recommendation thresholds vary by applicant demographics or discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of the written review (word count) is measured and used as a proxy for reviewer engagement or thoroughness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider length as an indicator of detail but control for verbosity differences by reviewer or language. Longer reviews may reflect more substantive critique but can also reflect style differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic patterns in review text
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific word choices, sentiment, and linguistic patterns in review text (e.g., adjectives used) are analyzed to detect bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply text-analysis techniques to identify differential use of praise/criticism across applicant groups. Control for reviewer native language and discipline-specific vocabulary to avoid confounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant gender (record & adjust)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant gender is recorded and tested as a potential source of bias in scores and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor score and recommendation differences by gender, including interaction effects with discipline and reviewer gender. Use anonymization or structured rubrics where appropriate to mitigate bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant age / career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant age or career stage is tracked as it influences evaluations (senior vs early-career effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about criteria appropriate for career stage; avoid using track-record expectations that systematically disadvantage early-career applicants. Consider separate rubrics or adjusted expectations for early-career proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant linguistic group / native language
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant linguistic group (German/French/Italian/International) is recorded; native-language applicants often receive slightly higher scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize writing-quality confounds with identity. Provide accommodations (e.g., editorial support) or explicit guidance to reviewers to focus on scientific content rather than language fluency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant discipline / field
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline or field of the application is a key contextual variable; bias patterns differ across fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design field-specific rubrics or weightings because a one-size-fits-all rubric may obscure differential bias. Compare like-with-like within disciplines when analyzing scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer gender (record & examine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer gender is recorded and analyzed; reviewer gender can influence critique patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether reviewer gender correlates with scores and whether female reviewers differ systematically in criticism. Use this information to understand reviewer heterogeneity and potential sources of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer geographic location
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer geographic location is captured as a contextual factor affecting judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether local vs international reviewers differ in scoring, possibly due to different standards or familiarity with local applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer–applicant gender interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The interaction between reviewer gender and applicant gender (same-gender vs cross-gender review) is examined for differential effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model interaction terms to detect subtle patterns (e.g., female reviewers more critical of female applicants in some fields). Do not assume homogeneity across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-specific rubric adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: One-size-fits-all rubrics may obscure differential bias; rubrics should be adapted to discipline-specific norms and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create discipline-tailored criteria and weighting schemes, and test for differential impacts across fields. Include field experts when designing rubrics to ensure relevant dimensions are captured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodation for non-native speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize linguistic/writing quality confounds and design rubrics or processes to avoid penalizing non-native speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement measures such as language-editing support, explicit reviewer guidance to focus on scientific merit, or separate checks that distinguish writing clarity from scientific quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias detection and monitoring at scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale monitoring and statistical testing can detect modest biases that are statistically significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement ongoing monitoring systems (e.g., analyses by gender, language, career stage) using sufficiently large datasets; interpret effect sizes in context and use results to guide policy (e.g., anonymization, reviewer training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of preliminary data in feasibility assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on preliminary data in assessing proposal quality is a recurring theme and can disadvantage applicants without extensive preliminary results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scoring feasibility, explicitly indicate acceptable forms of evidence for different career stages; consider alternative indicators (e.g., pilot analyses, simulations, strong rationale) to avoid penalizing early-career or resource-limited applicants.
